correctness.rationale: The rowwise two-point Hadamard transform separates the all-zero-character columns into the plus channel and sends the second frequency column at each \(t\) to exactly one exceptional plus row and otherwise to the minus channel. This gives the block operator \(\mathcal T=\begin{pmatrix}I&K\\0&I-K\end{pmatrix}\) with \(\|K\|^2=(p+1)/(2p)\le2/3\). Since \(\|K\|<1\), the inverse exists, and the stated norm bounds give squared condition number at most \((380+152\sqrt6)/3\approx250.774<251\). The actual verifier was inspected; it checks the channel assignment and exact endpoint arithmetic on representative odd primes, while the proof of the uniform theorem is analytic.

final_claim: For the Ferguson--Mayeli--Sothanaphan family \(E_p\subset \mathbb F_2^2\times\mathbb Z_p\), although its three fibers have no simultaneous exponential basis, the explicit frequency set \(B_p\) in the record is an exponential basis with \(\rho(E_p,B_p)<251\) for every odd prime \(p\ge3\); hence \(\rho(E_p)<251\) uniformly.
limitations: The constant \(251\) is not claimed optimal.
The argument is specific to this three-fiber family and does not remove the simultaneous-basis hypothesis from the general multi-tiling theorem.
